hourly.summary: A mixed bag of football vibes: Aston Villa's superclub aspirations get a reality check from The Athletic, while Manchester United's notebook reads like a worry list — Carrick's future, Lacey decisions, and UEFA fine fears. The Slovak post provides the only romance, an underdog manager told he lacked talent who started an era for the ages. United fans would settle for a fraction of that narrative right now.

daily.summary: Sentiment plummeted sharply across the day from cautious morning optimism about academy prospects and heritage to full-blown apocalyptic crisis mode by evening. The shift reflects escalating fury over managerial chaos, transfer incoherence, and deepening hatred toward the Glazer-Ratcliffe-Wilcox hierarchy, with fans now viewing Top 6 finishes as the ceiling of ambition.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a cataclysmic 2/10 crisis throughout the week, briefly punctuated only by a fleeting false dawn on October 28th when Kobbie Mainoo's return temporarily lifted spirits to 7/10 before injury setbacks and dressing-room fractures crashed the mood back to rock bottom. The dominant arc is one of deepening structural resignation: a nine-game winless streak, genuine relegation fears, unified fury at the Glazers and INEOS, and a pervasive belief that the squad has downed tools have calcified the fanbase into radioactive gallows humor and total abandonment of hope.
